interactions.label: Which of the following best describes India's annual corneal demand–supply gap?

params.question: Which of the following best describes India's annual corneal demand–supply gap?

answers.text: Approximately 50,000 corneas are needed and 40,000 are procured

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The actual need is far greater — India requires 150,000–200,000 donor corneas each year, not 50,000.

answers.text: Approximately 150,000–200,000 corneas are needed but only 30,000–40,000 are procured

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This massive gap means over 100,000 people who need keratoplasty lack access to a donor cornea annually.

answers.text: Approximately 30,000 corneas are needed and all are adequately procured

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 30,000–40,000 is the approximate number procured, not the number needed. The actual demand is several times higher.

answers.text: Approximately 500,000 corneas are needed but only 100,000 are procured

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While the gap is indeed large, the estimated annual need is 150,000–200,000 with only 30,000–40,000 procured.

overallFeedback.feedback: India needs 150,000–200,000 donor corneas each year but procures only 30,000–40,000 — leaving over 100,000 patients without access to keratoplasty.
Well done. The enormous gap between demand and procurement underscores why every potential corneal donation is critical.

params.question: After obtaining consent for eye donation, what is the recommended immediate bedside preservation technique?

answers.text: Instilling antibiotic eye drops and taping the eyelids closed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Antibiotics are not the priority at this stage. The immediate goal is preventing corneal desiccation by creating a moist chamber over closed lids.

answers.text: Closing the eyelids and placing moist sterile gauze pads over them to form a moist chamber

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The moist chamber protects both the corneal epithelium and endothelium from drying until the retrieval team can perform corneoscleral rim excision or enucleation.

answers.text: Packing the orbits with crushed ice to lower the corneal temperature rapidly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Ice is not applied directly to the orbits. Simple closure of the lids with moist sterile gauze creates the protective moist chamber needed.

answers.text: Irrigating the conjunctival sac with balanced salt solution

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Irrigation is unnecessary and impractical at the bedside. Moist sterile gauze over closed eyelids is the standard preservation measure.

overallFeedback.feedback: The correct technique is closing the eyelids and placing moist sterile gauze pads over them to form a moist chamber — this protects the cornea from desiccation until retrieval.
Exactly right. This simple, non-invasive step buys critical time by maintaining corneal hydration until the retrieval team arrives.

metadata.title: After obtaining consent for eye donation

interactions.label: Diabetes mellitus is an absolute contraindication to corneal donation.

params.question: Diabetes mellitus is an absolute contraindication to corneal donation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Diabetes does not prevent corneal donation. Absolute contraindications relate to transmissible pathogen risk — HIV, hepatitis B/C, rabies, prion diseases, and active septicaemia — not the severity of a systemic illness.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — diabetes is NOT a contraindication. The eye bank independently assesses corneal viability via specular microscopy. Absolute contraindications are limited to transmissible infections (HIV, hepatitis B/C, rabies, prion diseases) and active septicaemia.

params.question: A patient dies at a small rural hospital with no eye bank facility. The family has consented to corneal donation. What should the attending doctor do next?

answers.text: Attempt corneoscleral rim excision at the rural hospital

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Retrieval requires trained personnel and proper laboratory conditions — it should not be attempted without the appropriate setup.

answers.text: Close the eyelids, apply moist sterile gauze, refrigerate the body, and contact the eye bank hotline

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. These simple bedside measures maintain corneal viability while the eye bank coordinates retrieval, even from a remote location.

answers.text: Transport the body immediately to the nearest eye bank regardless of distance

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Long-distance transport is impractical and unnecessary. Bedside preservation with moist gauze and refrigeration extends the donation window effectively.

answers.text: Wait for the eye bank team to arrive without taking any interim preservation steps

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Waiting without preservation risks corneal desiccation and endothelial cell loss, potentially rendering the tissue unusable by the time the team arrives.

overallFeedback.feedback: The correct steps are: close the eyelids, apply moist sterile gauze, refrigerate the body, and contact the eye bank hotline. These simple measures preserve corneal viability until retrieval.
Well done. Even in resource-limited settings, these four simple steps — close lids, moist gauze, refrigerate, call the eye bank — can save two people's sight.
